title: What does the new evidence cast doubt on?
subtitle: Inferences · 17 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **17 of the official questions in Inferences are this one** — 1 Easy, 9 Medium, 7 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The passage opens with what scholars 'long thought' or what 'some interpret'.
- Then comes 'however' or 'but', followed by a new study.
- The blank sits right after words like 'casting doubt on the idea that' or 'challenging the assumption that'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Mark the old view and the evidence it rested on.
- 2) Check that the new data attacks that exact reasoning.
- 3) Choose the option that restates the old view, since that is what's being doubted, and not a new claim the study makes.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick something the new evidence supports, or a stronger claim the study never tested, when the blank wants the old idea being overturned.
The wrong answers often mention the right topic but attach to the wrong side of the 'however'.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
